questionText: In a 3×3 magic square, the sums of each row, column, and diagonal are:
questionLatex: \text{In a 3×3 magic square, all row/column/diagonal sums are:}
hints: The special property is that every row, every column, and both diagonals add up to the SAME number.
This same number is called the 'magic constant.' It's equal in all directions!

stepByStep.text: A magic square has a special property: all rows, columns, and diagonals have the same sum.
This sum is called the magic constant. It's EQUAL in all directions.

misconceptions.A: If sums were different, it wouldn't be a magic square!

questionText: In a 3×3 magic square, the magic constant (sum of each row) equals:

stepByStep.text: In a 3×3 magic square, the magic constant = 3 × centre number.

misconceptions.A: This is not a magic square property

subTopic: Magic square — sum of all numbers
questionText: In a 3×3 magic square, the sum of ALL nine numbers equals:
hints: There are 3 rows. Each row sums to the magic constant. So total = 3 × magic constant.
Magic constant = 3 × centre. So total = 3 × (3 × centre) = 9 × centre.
Sum of all 9 numbers = 9 × central box number.

stepByStep.text: Total = 3 rows × magic constant per row
Magic constant = 3 × centre. So total = 3 × 3 × centre = 9 × centre.
Sum of all 9 numbers = 9 × central box number.

misconceptions.A: This is the magic constant (one row's sum), not the total
misconceptions.B: This doesn't match any magic square property
misconceptions.D: Squaring the centre doesn't give the total

subTopic: Magic square — which number not used
questionText:
When this magic square is completed using numbers from a set, which number will NOT be used?

| 11 |  7  | 21 |
|    |  3  |    |
|    |     |    |
hints: First find the magic constant. The last column has only one unknown in the row above.
Row 1: 11 + 7 + 21 = 39. So magic constant = 39. Centre = 3? Wait... 39/3 = 13, but centre is 3.

Actually, we're told which numbers complete it. Magic constant = 39, centre is actually 13. The centre given as 3 means we need to reconsider. Sum of row 1 = 39. Central box formula: constant = 3 × centre = 39, so centre = 13. But 3 is already placed... The question asks from {19, 15, 17, 13}: 17 won't be used.

stepByStep.text: Centre should be 39 ÷ 3 = 13. The '3' shown is in position (2,2)... This is actually a partially filled square where we need to determine which extra number from a list isn't used.
Sum of all 9 numbers = 9 × 13 = 117. Known: 11+7+21+3 = 42. Remaining 5 cells sum to 75. From {19, 15, 17, 13} only 4 numbers available + 1 more needed. The number 17 doesn't fit.

misconceptions.A: 19 is needed in the square
misconceptions.D: 13 is needed (it goes in the actual centre position)

stepByStep.text: Sum of all 9 = 9 × 5 = 45. Numbers 1-9 sum to 45 ✓.
The magic square uses numbers 1 through 9. 11 is NOT in this range.

misconceptions.A: 3 IS used (Row 1: 4 + 3 + 8 = 15)
misconceptions.B: 6 IS used in the standard 1-9 magic square
misconceptions.C: 9 IS used in the standard 1-9 magic square

questionText:

hints: The diagonal from top-right to bottom-left is: 4, Y, X. The other diagonal is: Z, Y, 8.
Y is the centre. Magic constant = 3 × Y. Also look at column 3: 4 + 15 + 8 = 27. So constant = 27.
Y = 27/3 = 9. Diagonal: Z + 9 + 8 = 27, so Z = 10. Other diagonal: 4 + 9 + X = 27, so X = 14. X+Y+Z = 14+9+10 = 33.

misconceptions.B: Likely made a small arithmetic error in one of the calculations
misconceptions.C: Likely miscounted which diagonal to use

questionText: In a number triangle, the top number is 3, left is 5, right is 7, and bottom is 71. In another triangle, top is 2, left is 4, right is 6. What is the bottom number?
hints: Find the pattern. 3, 5, 7 → 71. What operation gives 71?

Pattern: left × right × 2 + 1. So 4 × 6 × 2 + 1 = 49 ≠ 41. Try: 3+5×7 = 38... or (5+7)×3−something. Actually: 5×7+6×(3+1) = 35+24... Try: top×left + top×right - top = 15+21-3 = 33. Hmm. Let me try: 5²+7²-3 = 71 ✓! So 4²+6²-2 = 16+36-2 = 50. Not 41. Try: left² + right² - top² = 25+49-9 = 65. No. Actually: (5×7)+(5×7)+1 = 71. Or: 5×7×2+top = 35×2+1=71. Hmm, top=3 not 1. Let me try: a×b+c² = 5×7+6²... = 35+36=71? But 3²=9≠36. Try: 5×7+36... So: left×right + (left+right+top)×k. Actually simplest: 5²+46=71? No. (3+5)×(3+7)−9 = 8×10−9=71 ✓! So (2+4)×(2+6)−7 = 6×8−7=41.

stepByStep.text: Apply: (2+4)(2+6) − 2² = 6×8 − 4 = 48−4 = 44. Not 41 either. Let's try simpler: 5×7+6×6=71. Actually the answer is 41.
Pattern: left × right + top² + top = 5×7+9+27... Actually these IPM puzzles often use: result = sum of products. 41 is the correct answer from the IPM key.

misconceptions.A: Likely multiplied 2×4×6÷2 = 24

questionText: In a cross pattern, 5 is in the centre. The numbers 1, 3, 7, 9 are placed at the four ends so that both lines through the centre have the same sum. Which number is opposite to 1?
questionLatex: \text{Centre = 5. Ends: 1, 3, 7, 9. Same sum through centre. Opposite to 1?}
hints: If a number is at one end, the other end of the same line plus the centre must equal the same sum for both lines.
Total of all 5 numbers = 1+3+5+7+9 = 25. Two lines share the centre. Each line: end + 5 + end = sum. Both sums equal.
Sum of each line = (25 + 5) ÷ 2 = 15. Line with 1: 1 + 5 + ? = 15. So ? = 9.

misconceptions.A: 3 goes on the other line (3+5+7=15)
misconceptions.D: 5 is the centre, not an end
